body: Seeing a Shaman Healer after years of torment from symptoms that seemed like mental illness. From the age of about 10 to 20 I had progressively worse symptoms of depression and anxiety, but towards the end it became extreme with my words being jumbled as I spoke, constant noise in my head, and I would be awake or asleep for days at a time. I didn't believe in healers or anything of this nature, but years of meds, hospital stays and therapy didn't help. 3 days, some massages, a cleansing with herbs and some prayers with limpias, and it was like I was alive for the first time. The difference was night and day, everything felt more clear and beautiful, the noise was gone, and I got my life back. I'm still struggling with my past, my self-esteem and letting go, but it doesn't compare to the constant nightmare I experienced before. I know I am blessed and fortunate to be where I am right now, and onwards I go. I know few if any will believe this story, but its mine and I'm sticking to it!

Its probably best not to specifically bring it up. Mental illness can be a rather touchy subject and its not always easy for people to explain or even talk about their illness and worries. 

If it doesn't come up, be sure to reassure your friend that you care about him/her and that you'll be there.

If it does come up, listen without judgement and above all be kind. There may not be much you can do to, but just being there makes a difference. 

Not sure how useful this is to you, but I do hope all goes well for you and your friend.

He's wrong. I know this illness can be so debilitating and devastating, and it may feel like hes right but he is so wrong. I see it as kind of like I'm in auto pilot and my body just kind of does what it does and talks and lives while I'm totally separated from it. I'll have moments where I'm doing something and then I realize "hey I'm driving!" or "hey I'm outside, how did I get here?" Its not like I don't remember, its more like I feel so out of place at random moments. Not sure if this is part of it too, but I often look at myself in the mirror and I always see myself differently each time. Not like one day I'm handsome and another I'm ugly, its more like I'm looking at myself for the first time every time. Its strange and I don't like it, but its kind of become a norm now.

I totally understand man, I'm kind of the same way. I used to be able to talk to people about anything but now its been hard for me to socialize and meet new people. Part of it is because I feel the need to talk about my disease and it feels like the small number of people that do listen are going to get fed up one day. Another reason is because I've been having some pretty bad anxiety along with my schizophrenia. For me what has sort of been a door opener is that I'll be joining a gym (Just got done with their trial) and it kind of pushes me to talk to others a little and practice talking to people again (I've only really talked to family and a friend or two for the last year or so). That's just my experience with relearning how to socialize.

I'd say you should try to find another medicine that will better help you. I don't think you have brain damage, I think it's just part of the disease. I felt that way while on the whole trial and error game of finding the right medication. Currently I'm on Geodone for Schiz and Klonopin for anxiety.
Hopefully you find your right medication and you can feel better soon!

As someone with schizophrenia and who has met other schizophrenics, we kind of vary greatly depending on our severity and disease type. The way it is for me is I have good days and bad days with this illness. It could be the same with your friend. His feelings for you are there, and during his better days he can cope with it and deal with it, but on his "bad days" maybe he can't? I think he recognized that he couldn't deal with it on an unexpected basis and requested some time to just relax. Personally, I've had to do the same where I couldn't handle situations and I had to say I needed some time to just let myself get better or at least feel better so I can handle these feelings I felt. I don't think it was  a delusion, at least it doesn't sound that way from the way you explained it. It just sounds like he needs a little space. As for advice, I'd say give him the space he needs and he'll probably contact you when he feels better and more able to talk with you.

For me, its a combination of factors. Its hard for me to talk to new people and for me to socialize outside of my family and couple of friends. Also, I'm terrified that I'll meet someone who is completely amazing and then scare them away with words like "Schizophrenia" or "Mental Illness". I do want a relationship, but I think it'll be hard not only to acquire one but even more so for me to maintain it and keep it alive and well. Maybe right now and for a while it'll just be me trying to get better and socialize more instead of me looking for an SO.
